findings.heading: ### F1. `index` unattended handling contradicts UNVERIFIED item 6 (blocking)
findings.body:
- Severity: MAJOR, graded blocking. Expert: Wiegers (consistency), Whittaker (Sequence/Divergence attack). Priority: High.
- Stated text A: section 3.2 `index` row, gate resolution column: "state that knowledge-base mode does not wait (whether it does is UNVERIFIED)" (`orca-worker-contract-spec.md:111`). The row's own parenthesis admits the fact is unknown; the inventory says the same: "no gate described, so whether it waits is UNVERIFIED" (`inventory/commands-a.md:54`, `:113`).
- Stated text B: UNVERIFIED item 6: "Whether `/sc:business-panel --mode socratic`, `/sc:explain --format interactive` and `/sc:index`'s knowledge-base mode wait for a person; section 3 refuses or pins them under `--unattended` regardless" (`orca-worker-contract-spec.md:277`).
- Grading sentence: an implementer who follows row `:111` as written adds one sentence to `/sc:index` saying knowledge-base mode does not wait, and builds an unattended mode that does not refuse or pin that mode; that is wrong because item 6 (`:277`) promises it is refused or pinned "regardless", WC-2 forbids any person-blocking step in unattended mode (`:60`), and a worker parked on a prompt is "healthy" and invisible to the coordinator (`CAPS:52`, `CAPS:129`, spec `:44`), so if the mode does wait the worker silently stalls with no `worker_done`. The other two modes in item 6 are handled as item 6 says (business-panel `--mode socratic` refused, `:102`; explain `--format interactive` refused, `:108`); `index` alone is not, so the two texts contradict.
- Recommendation: make the `index` row match its siblings (refuse or pin the knowledge-base mode under `--unattended`), or, if the mode is meant to stay allowed, change item 6 to say so and state how the fact will be verified before P1. Delete rather than add: the row text "state that ... does not wait" can be replaced by the same refuse/pin wording the two sibling rows use.
- Quality-impact estimate: low effort, removes the only unguarded silent-stall path among the P1 "no gate" commands.

findings.heading: ### B1 (CRITICAL, blocking) Phase 1 ships `--unattended` on 25 commands whose gates and outward defaults are converted only in later phases
findings.body:
- Experts: Whittaker (Sequence Attack), Wiegers, Nygard. Priority High.
- Attack: I can break this specification by **Sequence Attack**. The invariant at **WC-2 and WC-9 (`S:60`, `S:67`)** fails when **Phase 1 is shipped and Phase 2 is not yet shipped**. WC-2 says "Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question"; WC-9 says that under `--unattended` every default that pushes, posts to GitHub, installs or calls a paid run "is off". Both are stated without a phase qualifier.
- Stated text that conflicts: Phase 1 adds "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 except load (M3) (a no-op where a command has no gate)" and the contract (`S:159`); AC-1.1 asserts the `## Unattended mode` section for all of them (`S:195`). Gate conversion for those commands belongs to Phase 2, 3 or 4 (`S:160-162`; per-command phase column `S:99-125`). The spec also says each phase is "independently useful" (`S:154`) and that a later phase starts only when the earlier one passes (`S:154`), so the state "P1 shipped, P2 not" is a defined state.
- State trace (counts from the spec): flag accepted and section asserted for 36 commands (10 ready in `S:81-92` plus 27 changed in `S:99-125`, minus load, `S:159`, `S:195`). Live checks in AC-1.2 cover the P1 commands only: 8 (analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test) plus the 3 fixed ready commands (adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo), `S:159`, `S:196`, so 11. The remaining 25 get the flag with no live check and, for 22 of them, with the gate or outward default still in place (P2: 15, P3: 4, P4: 3 per `S:160-162`; the other 3 are brainstorm, init-lite, workflow which have no gate).
- Concrete wrong outcome: after Phase 1, a coordinator writes `/sc:auggie-review <PR> --unattended` into a worker brief, as `S:73` tells it to. The command accepts the flag, AC-1.1 passes (the section exists), and the command still posts a PR review and inline comments with "No confirmation prompt" and still ends on the remediation offer (`INV-A:38`; spec row `S:100`: the `--no-post-pr --no-remediation-offer` implication is Phase 2). That is an outward GitHub action under a flag WC-9 says switches such actions off, and a stalled worker under a flag WC-2 says removes every wait. The same holds after Phase 1 for cleanup and improve approval prompts (`S:103`, `S:110`), cli-eval's suite menu (`S:104`) and task's tier prompt (`S:121`).
- Why blocking: two stated texts contradict (WC-2/WC-9 unconditional versus the P1/P2 split) and an outward-action boundary is crossed (`INV-A:38`).
- Fix direction (repair only, no new mechanism): either make P1 add the flag only to the commands whose gate conversion is in the same phase, or state that `--unattended` on a command is not usable until that command's own phase has passed and make the P0 brief template list the commands that are usable.

findings.heading: ### F-01 (blocking, MAJOR) Phase 1 gives every command `--unattended` before the gate and outward-default changes that the flag promises
findings.body:
Experts: Wiegers (lead), Nygard, Whittaker (FR-2.4 Sequence Attack).

Grading sentence: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a Phase 1 in which gated commands accept `--unattended` and still prompt or post, and that is wrong because WC-2 and WC-9 say that under `--unattended` no prompt remains and every outward default is off.

Stated texts that meet:

- `spec:159` (P1): "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)". Its rationale is "No person gate is involved".
- `spec:195` (AC-1.1) asserts the `## Unattended mode` section on every command in 3.1 and 3.2 except load. That includes the P2 and P4 commands.
- `spec:196` (AC-1.2) runs the live check only on P1 commands. `spec:203` (AC-2.4, the auggie-review posting check) only exists in P2.
- `spec:60` (WC-2): under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends on a chat question. `spec:67` (WC-9): under `--unattended` any default that pushes, posts, installs or provisions is off.
- `spec:73` (2.3): the coordinator's brief states the exact command line "including `--unattended`".
- `spec:100`, `spec:121`, `spec:113`, `spec:114` (rows for auggie-review, task, post-release, pr-submit): the gate and outward-default changes are in P2 or P4. Their baseline is a default that posts to GitHub with no confirmation (`INV-A:38`, citing `cmd/auggie-review.md:51-54`, UNVERIFIED in the workspace), a TFEP report that is committed (`INV-B:204`), and installs/VM/commit/PR behind chat confirmations (`INV-B:79`).

State trace (auggie-review, Whittaker FR-2.4):

1. Before: P1 merged, P2 not started. `/sc:auggie-review` has the section and accepts `--unattended`. Posting is still the default, and the remediation offer is still a plain chat wait (`INV-A:62`).
2. The contract file from P0 (`spec:158`) and the brief template (`spec:73`) tell the coordinator to pass `--unattended` and that outward actions are off (`spec:67`).
3. The coordinator dispatches `/sc:auggie-review <PR> --unattended`.
4. After: review comments are posted to the PR (an outward action WC-9 says is off), and then the session ends its turn waiting on a reply nobody sends (a WC-2 stall with no `worker_done`, the exact failure `spec:44` calls invisible).

Nothing in the document marks the flag as not yet effective for these commands. P1 acceptance does not catch it, because the P1 checks never run a gated command. The same trace applies to `/sc:task` (commit/push EXEMPT keywords, `spec:121`), `/sc:post-release` and `/sc:implement`.

Same root cause, second symptom: `spec:241` (D3 recommendation (a)) says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4", and `spec:139` keeps pr-submit a worker candidate only if D3 is accepted. But P1 (`spec:159`) and AC-1.1 (`spec:195`) already require pr-submit to carry the section and the flag. Two stated texts cannot both hold under the recommended D3.

Recommendation: narrow P1 and AC-1.1 so that a command gains `--unattended` in the phase that makes the flag true for it (P1 for gate-free commands, P2 for the gated ones, P4 for the three decision-gated ones). If a command must accept the flag earlier, it should re

findings.heading: ### B-2 `--unattended` is made available to every command in P1, while the gate and outward-action rules it promises land in P2 to P4
findings.body:
- **Severity:** MAJOR (blocking; names a safety-boundary risk)
- **Expert:** Wiegers, Nygard
- **Priority:** High
- **Quality impact:** Consistency +2, safety of rollout
- **Grading sentence:** An implementer who follows the stated text as written ships P1 with `--unattended` accepted on all 37 commands (`SPEC:159`), each carrying an `## Unattended mode` section that names `return-contract.yaml` (`SPEC:195`), and the brief rule says to pass `--unattended` "from P1 on" (`SPEC:73`); but the rule that makes `--unattended` safe (WC-2: no prompt, WC-9: no outward default) is only built in P2 to P4 (`SPEC:100,109,113,114,121,160-162`). In that window `/sc:auggie-review <PR> --unattended` is accepted, still posts to GitHub with no confirmation (`SPEC:100`, `INV-A:38`), and then waits on a person, which is exactly what WC-2 and WC-9 say cannot happen under that flag.
- **Evidence:**
  - P1 scope (`SPEC:159`): "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)". It says nothing about a command that does have a gate.
  - AC-1.1 (`SPEC:195`) requires, in P1, a section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` on every 3.1 and 3.2 command except load. For P2 to P4 commands the contract and gate resolutions do not exist yet, so the P1 section would document behaviour not built.
  - Same pattern for implement (halt waits for a Ruling until P4, `SPEC:109`), post-release (confirmations until P4, `SPEC:113`), task (commit/push, `SPEC:121`), cli-eval (`SPEC:104`) and the ready rows whose gate fix is P2 (`SPEC:88-91`).
  - `SPEC:154` says phases are gated by checks, but no check stops a coordinator from using a command between phases; `SPEC:73` tells the coordinator to do so.
- **Recommendation:** narrow. In `SPEC:159`, `SPEC:195` and `SPEC:73`, limit P1 flag acceptance, the section and the "pass `--unattended`" instruction to the commands whose section-3 Phase column is P1 (and the P1 fixes of ready rows); each other command gains the flag and section in its own phase. If the flag must exist earlier, require a command whose gate conversion has not landed to refuse `--unattended` with a one-line message. Rationale: the flag then never claims a guarantee the command does not yet keep.

findings.heading: ### F-02 (blocking) Phase 1 ships `--unattended` on 37 commands while 19 of them still have an unconverted gate
findings.body:
- Experts: Martin Fowler (lead), Michael Nygard, Sam Newman.
- Location: `SPEC:154` ("Each phase is independently useful and leaves standalone behaviour unchanged"), `SPEC:159` (P1), `SPEC:160-162` (P2-P4), `SPEC:60` (WC-2), `SPEC:67` (WC-9), `SPEC:195` (AC-1.1).
- Stated text: P1 delivers "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)". The gates of the gated commands are converted in P2 (15 commands), P3 (4) and P4 (3) (`SPEC:160-162`).
- Pipeline Dimensional Analysis (FR-17 to FR-19; see the Quantity Flow Diagram below). P1 input is 37 commands that accept the flag (10 in 3.1 plus 27 in 3.2). Of these, 18 have no gate to convert, so a no-op is correct: the 9 P1 commands of 3.2, the 6 ready commands with no `--unattended` gate (adversarial, brainstorm, cleanup-audit, index-repo, init-lite, workflow), and save, validate-roadmap and validate-tests (drift fixes only). The other 19 accept the flag while their gate conversion lands later: 15 in P2 (11 from 3.2 plus reflect, release-split, tdd, troubleshoot), 1 in P3 (roadmap's resume prompt) and 3 in P4 (implement, post-release, pr-submit). Under FR-19 that 37-versus-18 mismatch is CRITICAL.
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows P1 as written, and then stops because "each phase is independently useful", ships `/sc:auggie-review --unattended` that is accepted but still posts to GitHub and then waits on a chat offer (the P2 row at `SPEC:100`; INV-A:38 shows both are default-on), and `/sc:post-release --unattended` that is accepted but still asks the pre-tag and outward-action questions (P4, `SPEC:113`). WC-2 says no person-blocking step under `--unattended`, and WC-9 says outward defaults are off under it; both are violated, and the first is an outward write to a third party. The parenthetical "(a no-op where a command has no gate)" does not say what the flag does where a command does have one, so a reader cannot tell whether those 19 are no-ops, refusals or full implementations.
- Whittaker attack (FR-2.4 Sequence Attack): see W-2.
- Recommendation: narrow P1 to the 18 commands without a gate, and make the flag land on each of the other 19 in the phase that converts its gate; or state that in P1 a gated command refuses `--unattended` with a clear message until its phase. Align AC-1.1 and the section 3 intro (`SPEC:76`) with the narrowed set.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Consistency 5 to 8, Safety posture 5 to 8.

findings.heading: ### F-1 (blocking, MAJOR): `--unattended` availability and guarantee are stated three incompatible ways; P1 gives it to commands whose gates are not resolved until P2-P4
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (consistency of requirements), Whittaker (Sequence Attack).
- Evidence. WC-2 says that under `--unattended` the command "never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question ... never says STOP AND WAIT" (spec:60). P1 says the phase delivers "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2" (spec:159), and AC-1.1 requires every command in 3.1 and 3.2 to have an `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` (spec:195). But the gate resolutions that WC-2 demands arrive later: P2 for 15 commands (spec:160), P3 for 4 (spec:161), P4 for implement, post-release and pr-submit (spec:162), and spec:154 says "Phases 1-3 need no user decision; Phase 4 waits for answers to D2-D4". The section a command gains lists "only its own gate resolutions" (spec:52); for implement, post-release and pr-submit those resolutions depend on D2, D3 and D4 (spec:109, 113, 114), and under D3(a), the recommended option, "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (spec:240) while AC-1.1 still requires a pr-submit section.
- Grading sentence. An implementer who follows P1 and AC-1.1 as written gives roughly 22 gate-bearing commands (for example `task`, `auggie-review`, `roadmap`, `implement`, `pr-submit`) an `--unattended` flag and an `## Unattended mode` section in P1, and the result is wrong because those commands then accept `--unattended`, pass AC-1.1, yet still prompt or wait on a person until P2 to P4, which is the silent stall WC-2 and spec:44 say the contract exists to prevent; for the P4 commands P1 would also have to write D2 to D4 outcomes that spec:154 says are not decided. AC-1.2 live-checks only the 13 P1 commands (spec:159, 196), so nothing in P1 catches it.
- Recommendation: state per phase which commands gain the flag and the section, and make the flag exist on a command only in the phase that resolves all of that command's gates; restrict AC-1.1 to the commands of that phase. Rationale: it removes the P1 contradiction by narrowing, not by adding mechanism, and keeps spec:154 true.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Consistency +2, Testability +1.

findings.heading: ### B-3 (BLOCKING). 7.2 step 5 fails on a worker that made no AskUserQuestion call
findings.body:
- Expert: Gojko Adzic (lead). Severity: MAJOR, blocking (the check fails on a conforming worker).
- Location: candidate:184 (step 5: "search the transcript for `AskUserQuestion`. Pass: no `AskUserQuestion` call."); candidate:60 (WC-2 requires the contract to say the command "never calls `AskUserQuestion`"); candidate:52 and :158 (the contract file is `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` and carries the section 2 rules); candidate:51-52 (every changed command's Unattended section points to it).
- Issue: the check is a text search of the transcript. The worker reads the contract (it is named in every Unattended section), and the contract's own text contains the string "AskUserQuestion" (WC-2 quotes it). Command files that describe their gates also contain it (for example INV-A:44 on cli-eval's AskUserQuestion menu). The step as written does not limit the search to tool-call entries, so a conforming worker returns a hit.
- Grading check: "An implementer who follows step 5 as written searches the whole transcript for the string, and the worker's read of the contract (required by candidate:60 and :52) returns a hit, so step 5 fails on a worker that made no call."
- Recommendation: search tool_use entries whose name is `AskUserQuestion`, not the raw transcript text. State the transcript paging (F-8).
- Priority: High. Quality impact: every P1-P4 live check (7.2 step 5) fails on a correct run, so the phase gates cannot pass.

findings.heading: ### B2 (CRITICAL, blocking) cli-portify cannot pass its own happy-path acceptance check
findings.body:
- Experts: Wiegers (testability), Adzic (examples), Whittaker (Zero/Empty Attack). Priority High.
- Attack: I can break this specification by **Zero/Empty Attack** on the approval input. The invariant at **cli-portify row (`S:105`) with WC-2 (`S:60`) and AC-2.3 (`S:201`)** fails when **the coordinator supplies every flag the row lists**.
- Stated text: the row resolves "each of the three approval gates ... as blocked with the artifact to review named in the contract", and adds only a `--resume <contract>` flag that "uses the existing `resume_phase`/`resume_substep` fields" (`S:105`). WC-2 allows three resolutions per gate: a default, a caller-supplied flag, or blocked (`S:60`); the row picks only the third for all three gates. AC-2.3 requires, for every P2 command, "Happy-path run ... with every required flag in the brief" that ends `--outcome succeeded` (`S:201`). WC-3's route (ask the coordinator, then "re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag", `S:61`) names no flag by which an approval can be passed.
- State trace: run 1 reaches the first approval gate (after Phases 1 and 2, `INV-A:45`) and ends `status: blocked`, `--outcome failed` (`S:63`). Run 2, `--resume <contract>`, restarts at the saved phase and meets the same gate, because no input carries the approval. Any number of resumes ends the same way. The three gates sit at `INV-A:45` (before Phase 3, before delivery).
- Concrete wrong outcome: an implementer follows the row exactly and builds a command that can never end `succeeded` under `--unattended`; AC-2.3 cannot pass for it; Phase 2 cannot be declared done (`S:154`).
- Why blocking: a stated text that an acceptance criterion cannot pass (FIRST-REVIEW grading check, `document_review_loop_prompts.md:31`).
- Fix direction: give the row a caller-supplied approval input for the three gates (WC-2 option b), or exclude cli-portify from AC-2.3 and say that it is a human-in-the-loop command.

=== ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS ===

Architecture verdict (Fowler, Newman, Hohpe, Nygard): the central decision is sound and well evidenced. Orca coordinates and commands stay units of work (`S:16`); no Orca call in a command (`S:213`, SA-2 `S:147`); the rejected alternative is argued from the depth fence (`CAPS:97-101`), standalone use (`CAPS:147-149`), completion ownership (`CAPS:76`, `CAPS:150`) and the executable name (`CAPS:145`); the evidence-strength limits are stated honestly (`S:41-45`). The shared-contract-file design (one document, per-command section, `S:52`) keeps the write-once rule. The interface between the coordinator and a worker is one file plus one flag, which is a narrow, stable seam (Newman). The report-file seam has the following gaps, none blocking on its own: M2, M3, M13 below.

Fowler (interface and boundaries): the six coordinator-only commands (`S:130-137`) track the inventories (`INV-A:36,49,50`; `INV-B:32,42,44`). Totals reconcile: 43 = 10 + 27 + 6 (`S:76`; `INV-A:73`; `INV-B:278`). Nygard (failure modes): see M4 (liveness), M3 (retry), M13 (blocked-then-failed). Hohpe (message flow): the lifecycle messages are correctly confined to the top-level session (`S:65`); the ask / reply / check loop is consistent with

findings.heading: ### F3 - CRITICAL (blocking) - Adzic - cli-portify: the happy-path check cannot pass, because every gate resolves only as blocked
findings.body:
- Texts: cli-portify row: "each of the three approval gates resolves as blocked", resume via `--resume <contract>` (`SPEC:105`); the gates are always on (A:45); WC-2 allows three resolutions (default, caller flag, blocked) (`SPEC:60`), but the row picks only the third and lists no flag that carries an approval; AC-2.3: "Happy-path run per P2 command with every required flag in the brief ... 7.2 passes with `--outcome succeeded`" (`SPEC:201`) and P2 contains cli-portify (`SPEC:160`).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a cli-portify that stops as blocked at the first approval gate on every unattended run and, on resume, reaches the same gate again, because no listed flag or contract field records an approval; AC-2.3 requires a `succeeded` run, which that build can never produce.
- Recommendation: either name the approval input (one flag, resolution (b) of WC-2) in the cli-portify row, or narrow AC-2.3 to say cli-portify's expected unattended result is `blocked` / `failed` at the first gate. Prefer the AC-2.3 narrowing.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Completeness +1, Testability +2.

findings.heading: ### B-1 (CRITICAL, blocking) Wiegers / Cockburn: `--unattended` is made accepted by 36 commands in P1, while the behaviour it promises arrives for 22 of them in P2-P4
findings.body:
Priority: High. Quality impact: safety and stall risk in P1-P3.
Texts that collide:
- S:159 (P1 scope): "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 except `load` (a no-op where a command has no gate)". That is 10 + 26 = 36 commands.
- S:73 (section 2.3): the brief carries "`--unattended` only for a command that already accepts it in the phase being run".
- S:60 (WC-2): under `--unattended` the command "never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question", and WC-9 (S:67) turns every push, PR, post, install, provision and paid call off.
- S:109-113, S:114, S:162 and S:154: the gate resolutions for implement, post-release and pr-submit are P4 and "wait for answers to D2-D4"; the 15 P2 commands convert in P2 (S:160); roadmap, save, validate-roadmap, validate-tests in P3 (S:161).
Quantity flow (FR-19, count divergence): 36 commands accept the flag after P1; 14 are behaviourally complete (8 no-gate P1 rows other than `load`, plus adversarial, brainstorm, cleanup-audit, index-repo, init-lite, workflow). 22 accept it with the gate or outward default still as today (15 until P2, 4 until P3, 3 until P4).
Sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written adds `--unattended` to `/sc:post-release`, `/sc:pr-submit`, `/sc:task`, `/sc:cleanup` and `/sc:tdd` in P1, and a coordinator who follows section 2.3 passes it to them in P1-P3 because they "accept it"; that is wrong because WC-2 and WC-9 promise no prompt and no outward action under that flag, yet post-release still confirms and performs install, VM, commit and PR steps and the others still stop on a prompt the coordinator cannot see (a silent stall, S:60, CAPS:129), until P2-P4.
Why the acceptance checks do not catch it: AC-1.1 (S:195) tests only that a `## Unattended mode` section exists and names two strings; AC-1.2 (S:196) live-checks P1 commands only.
Recommendation (narrow, no new mechanism): in S:159 and S:73 state that a command accepts `--unattended` only in the phase that converts its own gates (the section 3 "Phase" column), or that before that phase the command refuses the flag with `status: blocked`. Delete "a no-op where a command has no gate" if it is not needed.

findings.heading: ### B1 [MAJOR, blocking] `--unattended` is promised to mean "no person, no outward default" but the phase plan ships it before the gates exist
findings.body:
- **Grading sentence.** An implementer who follows the stated text builds Phase 1 as written (`SPEC:159`, `SPEC:195`): `--unattended` and a `## Unattended mode` section on every command of sections 3.1 and 3.2 except `/sc:load`. Phases 2 to 4 convert the gates later (`SPEC:160-162`). The result after Phase 1 is a command such as `/sc:auggie-review` that accepts `--unattended`, still posts to GitHub by default and still offers remediation and waits (`INV-A:38`, `SPEC:100` marks that change P2). That is wrong because WC-2 says "under `--unattended` the command never calls AskUserQuestion, never ends its turn on a chat question" (`SPEC:60`) and WC-9 says "under `--unattended`, any default that pushes, opens a PR, posts to GitHub ... is off" (`SPEC:67`). The text also calls each phase "independently useful" (`SPEC:154`), and the contract file that states WC-2 and WC-9 for every command lands in P0 (`SPEC:158`), so a coordinator that trusts the flag can dispatch `--unattended` at P1 and trigger an outward post or a stall.
- **Second contradiction in the same place.** AC-1.1 asserts that every command in 3.1 and 3.2 except load has the section (`SPEC:195`), which includes `/sc:pr-submit`. D3(a), the recommendation, says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" and section 4 says pr-submit is a worker candidate "only if the user accepts D3" (`SPEC:240`, `SPEC:139`). So AC-1.1 forces a pr-submit change that D3(a) rules out; the same holds for `/sc:implement` and `/sc:post-release`, whose unattended behaviour waits on D2 and D4 (`SPEC:154`, `SPEC:109`, `SPEC:113`) while the P1 test already requires their sections. Section 2.1 says each section "lists only its own gate resolutions" (`SPEC:52`), which for those commands do not exist at P1.
- **Expert.** Wiegers (consistency of requirements), Fowler (phase boundary and interface), Whittaker (sequence attack, see W1).
- **Recommendation.** Narrow, do not add: attach the flag and section to a command in the phase named in its own row (P1 only for the no-gate commands and the four ready-command fixes), and restrict AC-1.1 to the commands whose phase has landed. Say that pr-submit, implement and post-release get no section until their decision (D3, D2, D4) is made. Rationale: the flag then never claims a guarantee its command cannot yet keep.
- **Priority.** High. **Quality impact.** Consistency +2, safety of the worker boundary.

findings.heading: ### F-01 (CRITICAL-adjacent MAJOR, blocking) Sequence attack: P1 makes `--unattended` available on commands whose gates only convert in P2-P4
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (lead), Whittaker (Sequence Attack), Cockburn.
- Where: spec:159 (P1: "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)", refusing only auggie-review, task, pr-submit, post-release), spec:73 (the coordinator brief includes `--unattended` "from P1 on"), spec:60 (WC-2: under `--unattended` the command never prompts), spec:44 (section 1.4 item 2: a command prompt is a silent stall with no `worker_done`), spec:160-162 (gate conversion lands in P2, P3, P4).
- Grading check: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, at the end of P1, `/sc:cleanup`, `/sc:improve`, `/sc:cli-eval`, `/sc:cli-portify`, `/sc:tdd`, `/sc:troubleshoot`, `/sc:roadmap`, `/sc:review-translation`, `/sc:implement` and about ten more that accept `--unattended` and still stop on their approval gates; section 2.3 then tells the coordinator to pass `--unattended` to every worker from P1 on; and the worker parks on a prompt nobody can answer, which is exactly what WC-2 forbids and section 1.4 item 2 calls the real failure mode. The text needs no further assumption: P1 names only four commands to refuse, and every other gated command falls under "accepted".
- I can break this specification by **Sequence Attack**. The invariant at **WC-2 (spec:60)** fails when **a phase boundary is crossed in the middle of the rollout**. Concrete attack: state after P1 = {cleanup: flag accepted, gate "Approval Required" unchanged}; coordinator brief per spec:73 = `/sc:cleanup <dir> --unattended --output <dir>`; worker reaches the approval step (`commands-a.md:43`); state after = worker waiting, no `worker_done`, `worker-show` `agentWait` non-null (spec:189). The P1 acceptance check AC-1.2 (spec:204) tests only the P1 commands, so nothing catches it.
- Recommendation: extend the P1 refusal rule (spec:159) from "outward default" commands to every command whose gate converts in a later phase, until that phase lands, and state in spec:73 that the brief uses `--unattended` for a command only once its phase has landed. This narrows the flag surface rather than adding a mechanism.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: Testability and Consistency, about +2.

findings.heading: ### B-01. Phase 1 makes `--unattended` accepted by all 37 commands before the gates and outward defaults it promises are honoured
findings.body:
- Stated text: P1 adds "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)" (S:159). WC-2 and WC-9 say that under `--unattended` no gate waits and every pushing, posting or committing default is off (S:60, S:67). The section 3 rows put the actual resolutions in later phases: auggie-review posting, `/sc:task` `commit`/`push` and the committed TFEP report in P2 ("P2 only turns it off under `--unattended`", S:160, S:100, S:121), pr-submit HALTs and post-release in P4 (S:114, S:113, S:162).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows S:159 then S:160/S:162 as written ships, after P1, commands that accept `--unattended` and still post to GitHub (auggie-review, S:100; INV-A:38 shows the default posts with no prompt), commit and push (task EXEMPT keywords, S:121; INV-B:45) or ask a person (cleanup, improve, cli-portify, S:103/105/110). The coordinator brief (S:73) always puts `--unattended` on the command line, so the coordinator reads the flag as "safe, no person, no outward action". That behaviour is wrong because WC-9 is false in that state, and the effect is an outward action (a posted review, a push) on a command the brief believed was quiet.
- The spec never says a coordinator must not dispatch a command before its phase lands, and the P0 brief template lists only the section 3.1 flags (S:158), so nothing blocks the dispatch.
- Attack trace (Whittaker, sequence): State after P1 passes: auggie-review accepts `--unattended`, section says nothing yet. Step 1: coordinator dispatches `/sc:auggie-review 42 --unattended`. Step 2: command runs its default (post to PR, then wait on the remediation offer, INV-A:38, INV-A:62). Before: no review on PR 42. After: review and inline comments posted, worker stalled with no `worker_done`.
- Recommendation: until a command's resolutions land, it must refuse `--unattended` (fail closed with `status: blocked`), or P1 must limit the flag to the 15 commands whose full resolution lands in P1. Narrow, do not add a mechanism.

findings.heading: ### B-3 (MAJOR, blocking, High): P1 adds `--unattended` to gated, outward-acting commands before their gate conversion
findings.body:
Experts: Nygard, Whittaker (Sequence Attack, FR-2.4), Fowler.
Texts that conflict:
- P1 delivers "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)" (spec:159). Gate conversion is P2 (spec:160), drift fixes P3, and implement, post-release and pr-submit are P4 (spec:162). Section 2.3 tells the coordinator to put `--unattended` in every brief (spec:73); WC-2 and WC-9 define the flag as "no person-blocking step" and "any default that pushes, opens a PR, posts, installs ... is off" (spec:60, 67).
- auggie-review posts to the PR by default with no prompt (`cmd/auggie-review.md:51-54` via spec:67, `INV-A:98`); post-release has VM, real-target install, commit and PR steps (spec:113).
Wrong outcome: after P1 an implementer has built a flag that auggie-review, cleanup, task, post-release and pr-submit accept but ignore until P2 or P4. A coordinator that follows 2.3 passes `--unattended` believing WC-9 holds, and auggie-review posts to the PR and ends its turn on the chat offer (`INV-A:62`). It is wrong because the flag's stated meaning (WC-2, WC-9) is not true for those commands, and the phase text says the flag is accepted while "each phase is independently useful" (spec:154). The result is an outward action under a flag that promises none, which is a safety-boundary risk.
Recommendation (Nygard): in P1 accept the flag only for commands whose gate and outward-default resolutions ship in the same phase; before that phase the command should refuse `--unattended` (fail closed). State this in the P1 and P2 rows.
Quality impact: Completeness +1, safety of the rollout +3.

findings.heading: #### R1-B1. CRITICAL, blocking. Phase P1 contradicts WC-2 and the phase and decision structure
findings.body:
- **Expert**: Wiegers, confirmed by Fowler. **Priority**: High. **Quality impact**: consistency -2, testability -1.
- **Grading sentence**: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, in Phase 1, an `--unattended` flag and a `## Unattended mode` section on all 37 commands of sections 3.1 and 3.2, including gated ones (task, cleanup, cli-eval, roadmap, implement, post-release, pr-submit); each accepts the flag while still prompting, and X is wrong because WC-2 says that under `--unattended` the command never prompts, and AC-1.1 passes on the mere presence of the section, so nothing in P1 detects the stall.
- **Contradicting texts**:
  - P1 scope: "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)" (spec line 159); AC-1.1 asserts the section exists "for every command in sections 3.1-3.2" (line 195).
  - Section 6 assigns gate conversion to P2 (line 160), interface drift to P3 (line 161) and implement, post-release and pr-submit to P4 (line 162), with P4 waiting on D2 to D4 (lines 154, 162, 225).
  - WC-2: "Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question ... Each gate resolves one of three ways" (line 60).
  - Section 2.1: each section "lists only its own gate resolutions" (line 52). For implement, post-release and pr-submit those resolutions are defined only by the unresolved D2 to D4 (lines 109, 113, 114).
  - D3(a), the recommendation, says "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (line 240) yet pr-submit is one of the 27 commands "needing a change" (line 76) and AC-1.1 requires its section at P1.
- **Wrong outcome (state trace)**: after P1, installed `/sc:task` and `/sc:cleanup` accept `--unattended` and name a contract (AC-1.1 passes); a coordinator reads `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, dispatches `/sc:task "<x>" --unattended` with confidence 0.65; the command still prompts (the P2 conversion is not built), the worker parks silently with no `worker_done`, which the spec itself says is invisible (line 44; `CAPS:52,129`).
- **Recommendation**: state which behaviour each phase adds per command (flag plus contract only, or gate handling too), and either narrow AC-1.1 and the P1 scope to the P1 command set or make a command refuse `--unattended` (resolve as blocked) until its gate conversion phase.

findings.heading: ### F2 (BLOCKING, MAJOR) Phase 1 requires the unattended mode on commands whose rules the spec defers to Phases 2-4 and to user decisions
findings.body:
- Expert: Wiegers (requirements consistency), Cockburn (who decides what, when), Fowler (phase boundaries).
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, in Phase 1, an accepted `--unattended` flag and `## Unattended mode` section on `implement`, `post-release`, `pr-submit` (and on the gated Phase 2 commands such as `auggie-review` and `task`) with no gate resolution behind it, and that is wrong because WC-2/WC-9 say that under `--unattended` no prompt waits and no outward default fires, and section 6 says the gate rows land in P2 and P4 after D2-D4.
- Evidence:
  - P1 scope (`:159`): "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)". Section 3.1-3.2 includes the P2 and P4 commands.
  - AC-1.1 (`:195`) makes the P1 test assert the section for every one of those commands.
  - Section 6 intro (`:154`): "Phases 1-3 need no user decision; Phase 4 waits for answers to D2-D4". The P4 commands' unattended behaviour is exactly what D2 (`:232-236`), D3 (`:238-242`), D4 (`:244-247`) decide.
  - D3 recommends (a), "no pr-submit changes in Phase 4" (`:240`), and section 4 (`:139`) makes `/sc:pr-submit` a worker candidate only if D3 is accepted. P1 as written still gives `pr-submit` the flag and the section.
  - WC-9 (`:67`) and the `auggie-review` row (`:100`): under `--unattended` the PR-posting default is off. In P1 the flag exists but (per the row's phase P2, `:100`) that behaviour does not yet, so a coordinator briefing `auggie-review --unattended` after P1 still posts to GitHub and waits on the remediation offer.
- Why blocking: two stated texts contradict (P1 scope and AC-1.1 against section 6's phase split and WC-2/WC-9), and the intermediate state they produce is the unsafe one the contract exists to prevent.
- Recommendation: narrow P1 and AC-1.1 to the commands whose section 3 row has phase P1 (plus the P1 fixes to ready commands); let each later phase add the flag and section together with its gate rows.
- Priority: High. Quality impact: about 0.5 of a Consistency point.

=== ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS ===

No blocking architecture finding. The central decision (Orca coordinates; commands stay units of work; section 1.3 rejects commands calling Orca) is supported by `CAPS:97-103`, `CAPS:145-150` and `INV-A:90`, and section 1.4 states the evidence gaps honestly (Phase 0 smoke runs close the main one).

findings.heading: ### F-1 [MAJOR, blocking] Phase 1 ships `--unattended` on commands whose person-gates are only converted in Phase 2-4, while the coordinator is told to pass it from Phase 1 on
findings.body:
Experts: Wiegers (requirement conflict), Nygard (a silent stall is the worst failure), Whittaker (Sequence attack).

Grading sentence. An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds, in Phase 1, an `--unattended` flag that is accepted by every command in 3.1 and 3.2 except four (`SPEC:159`), and the coordinator brief template tells coordinators to pass `--unattended` "from P1 on" (`SPEC:73`). The gate conversions for `cleanup`, `improve`, `cli-eval`, `cli-portify`, `recommend`, `research`, `review-translation`, `spec-panel`, `tasklist`, `reflect`, `release-split`, `tdd`, `troubleshoot` are assigned to P2 (`SPEC:100,103-105,110,115-117,120,122`, `SPEC:160`); `roadmap`, `save`, `validate-*` to P3 (`SPEC:118-119,124-125`, `SPEC:161`); `implement` to P4 (`SPEC:109`, `SPEC:162`). So after P1 a coordinator that dispatches `/sc:cleanup <dir> --unattended` gets a command that accepts the flag and still prompts "Approval Required" (`SPEC:103` quotes the gate; `INV-A:43`). WC-2 says that under `--unattended` the command "never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question" (`SPEC:60`). The result is a worker parked on a prompt with no `worker_done`, which Orca reports as "healthy, not failed" (`CAPS:52`, `CAPS:129`) and which the spec itself calls "invisible" (`SPEC:60`). It is wrong because the spec has no stated text under which the flag is accepted but the gate stays; each phase is declared "independently useful" and shippable alone (`SPEC:154`, `SPEC:156`).

The text itself shows the authors saw the problem for outward defaults: four commands "refuse it with an error until their P2 or P4 change lands" (`SPEC:159`, M3). The same refusal is not applied to the stall class. `SPEC:159` reads "(a no-op where a command has no gate)", which under one reading means gated commands do something in P1, contradicting their P2-P4 assignment; under the other it means they stay prompting. Either reading contradicts WC-2 or section 6.

Also: AC-1.1 asserts a `## Unattended mode` section in every 3.1-3.2 command at P1 (`SPEC:203`), but the section "lists only its own gate resolutions" (`SPEC:52`), which do not exist until P2-P4. AC-1.2 live-checks only the P1 command list (`SPEC:204`, `SPEC:159`), so nothing in P1 catches a gated command accepting the flag.

Recommendation (for the reviser, narrow only): extend the P1 refusal rule from the four outward-default commands to every command whose section 3 row has a non-"no gate" resolution assigned to a later phase, until that phase lands; or move the flag to the phase that converts the gate. Priority: High. Quality impact: Completeness and Consistency, about 1.5 points each.

findings.heading: ### F-1 (blocking) Phase 1 text contradicts WC-2 and section 2.3 for every command whose gate converts in a later phase
findings.body:
- Severity: MAJOR, graded blocking. Experts: Wiegers, Adzic, Nygard.
- Grading sentence: An implementer who follows the stated text as written builds Phase 1 so that `--unattended` is accepted by cleanup, improve, cli-eval, cli-portify, task, tdd, troubleshoot, implement, post-release, pr-submit and the other gated commands while their gates are still live, and X is wrong because WC-2 says "Under `--unattended` the command never calls `AskUserQuestion`, never ends its turn on a chat question ..." and section 2.3 tells the coordinator to pass `--unattended` for "a command that already accepts it in the phase being run", so the coordinator passes the flag, the command still stops on a person-only prompt, and the worker stalls silently with no `worker_done` (the stall mode the spec itself describes at spec line 44).
- Evidence (two stated texts that contradict each other):
  - `specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md:159`: P1 delivers "the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 except `load` ... (a no-op where a command has no gate)". Gate resolution for gated commands is scheduled in P2 (`:160`), P3 (`:161`) and P4 (`:162`), and the section 3.2 Phase column agrees (for example cleanup `:103` P2, pr-submit `:114` P4, implement `:109` P4).
  - `specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md:60`: WC-2 has no phase carve-out.
  - `specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md:73`: the coordinator passes the flag only where "it already accepts it in the phase being run". After P1 every command accepts it, so the condition is satisfied for commands whose gate still prompts.
  - `specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md:195` (AC-1.1) requires every command in 3.1-3.2 to carry a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` in P1, including pr-submit, post-release and implement, whose gate and outward-action rules wait for decisions D2-D4 (`:154`, `:162`).
  - The "no-op where a command has no gate" parenthesis does not cover gated commands, and P1's own list of commands (`:159`) names only the no-gate ones as "commands", so the sentence reads both ways. The scope sentence and the section 3 phase column cannot both hold.
- Recommendation: narrow P1 to "accepted by the commands whose section 3 phase is P1, plus the no-gate ready commands"; each command then gains the flag in the phase named in its section 3 row; state in 2.3 that the flag is passed only after the command's own phase has passed. Delete rather than add: this is a scope narrowing of one sentence plus AC-1.1.
- Priority: High.

findings.heading: **F-07. Two ready-today commands can stall with no `worker_done`.**
findings.body:
§3.1 (line 81) says the ready commands "run as workers now if the brief uses the stated flags". Two rows depend on prompts that the stated flags do not stop:
- tdd (line 90): the nested `/task` "ask the user" lines are unflagged until P2 (the row says so). `/task` asks when several task files match (INV-B:219, citing sk/task/SKILL.md:49). The brief's precise prompt and `--output` do not prevent this.
- troubleshoot (line 91): the `--depth deep` short-input STOP that asks the user is unflagged until P2 (INV-B:239, citing sk/sc-troubleshoot-protocol/SKILL.md:57). A brief that uses `--depth deep` with a short input stalls.
An implementer who follows §3.1 dispatches these and gets a silent stall, which WC-2 says must not happen and which the coordinator sees only through `agentWait` (§7.2 step 2).
Fix: list the triggering inputs in the "Brief must pass" column (for tdd, a specific component with a known task file; for troubleshoot, no `--depth deep`), or move both rows out of ready-today until P2.
